operator_request: Proceed with the recommended narrow wreq dependency path after WP-007 returned FAILED_SPIKE_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_DECISION.

current_primary_sources.evidence: Official source documents fine-grained TLS and HTTP/2 emulation, browser profiles, proxy and pooling support, BoringSSL build requirements, optional symbol prefixing, and its status as a hard fork of reqwest.
The current v6 line is 6.0.0-rc.29 rather than a stable 6.0 release.

The current stable documentation is wreq 5.3.0 and documents disabled-by-default redirects, optional cookies, enabled system-proxy discovery unless no_proxy is selected, streaming bodies, HTTP/2, TLS, and pool controls.
Rustls maintainers closed ClientHello fingerprint exposure as not planned, confirming the measured pure-Rust gap is not addressed by the baseline stack.

selected_approach: Authorize only FF-DEC-001, scoped to the non-shipped fforager-transport consumer.
Compile and exercise stable wreq 5.3.0 as a control before retaining or rejecting exact-pinned v6.0.0-rc.29.
Keep Ferric's WP-007 candidate contract as the capability, policy, security, bounds, transcript, and verdict authority.
Disable wreq ambient proxy discovery, automatic redirects, cookie store, and transparent decompression in the candidate builder.
Separate deterministic local evidence from explicitly opt-in live fingerprint reflection evidence.
Reject production promotion until a separate Operator decision and shipped-artifact runtime proof.
rejected_options: Reqwest/rustls as the sole path because it does not close the measured browser fingerprint blocker.
Curl-impersonate/libcurl because it adds a less Rust-aligned patched C integration and larger packaging/IPC surface.
Chromium/CDP because the default transport does not require a full browser runtime and the resource/lifecycle cost is substantially larger.
Craftls or an in-tree TLS/H2 fork because Ferric would assume security-critical browser-profile and wire maintenance.
A dual production backend during this packet because no shipped transport is authorized and the additional pool/policy divergence would not improve dependency adjudication.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Profile configuration is falsely reported as wire parity.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Record configured profile separately from negotiated protocol and externally observed fingerprint; live proof is opt-in and cannot be synthesized from configuration.
Disable ambient proxies, redirects, cookies, and decompression in the builder; preserve Ferric-owned typed policy inputs and add construction-time negative tests.
Pin versions, enumerate exact Cargo links/build scripts/features/sources, enable symbol prefixing when available, reject unlisted consumers and native links, and inspect clean artifacts.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: The release candidate changes or profiles become stale.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Bind reports to exact crate/source/profile identities and require a dedicated validated update; prefer stable 5.3.0 if it passes the same required evidence.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: A non-shipped success is treated as product progress.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Retain the prerequisite zero-progress declaration, runtime-truth ceiling, and explicit product-promotion prohibition in FF-DEC-001.

basis.validation_plan: Build and exercise the stable control and exact-pinned release candidate through the same public candidate boundary; inspect exact dependency/build/native surfaces; run deterministic local and opt-in live fingerprint probes, policy-negative tests, bounds/cancellation/sanitizer tests, behavior-changing counterfactuals, architecture/runtime/deep/PR gates, and three independent adversarial implementation reviews; remediate confirmed findings with public-boundary regressions and rerun the complete matrix.

assumptions: The Operator authorization is intentionally limited to the recommended non-shipped adjudication step and does not silently promote BoringSSL into Ferric product packages.
Canonical verification must remain able to run without internet access; live fingerprint reflection is additional opt-in evidence.
A candidate may pass dependency adjudication while residual product-integration work remains explicit.
non_goals: Full browser, extractor, or replacement parity.
Replacing Ferric policy with dependency defaults.

attack_lenses: TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprint evidence integrity
DNS, peer-address, proxy, and SSRF evidence gaps
pool partition and cancellation lifecycle leakage
native build, symbol, source, artifact, and license expansion
false product promotion or proof-class inflation
minimum_controls: At least two implementation-independent checks beyond the implementer's command list.
Concrete counterfactuals for capability gating and native exception enforcement.
Producer-consumer boundary probes for adapter reports and architecture policy.
Negative paths for unsupported profiles, ambient proxy configuration, missing wire receipt, wrong native consumer, extra native link, timeout, cancellation, and secret canaries.
Every confirmed finding becomes a public-boundary regression before closure.

execution_decomposition: Activate FF-DEC-001 and the WP-015 prerequisite packet.
Resolve and record stable and release-candidate dependency graphs.
Implement the capability-gated wreq adapter and report schema.
Run deterministic local, opt-in live, dependency, bounds, cancellation, and counterfactual probes.
Run canonical gates and independent adversarial implementation reviews.
Remediate findings, simplify, rerun, record the adjudication verdict, and preserve the zero-progress ceiling.
